Subject: Recap & next steps — offline/on-prem qualification

Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on your air-gapped/on-prem requirements:

Summary from our call:
- Deployment mode: Private (air-gapped) on-prem appliance behind customer network boundary.
- Primary concerns: offline upgrades, zero egress, hardware spec validation, operator runbook for upgrades and failover.
- Timeline: target pilot in Q1 2027, depending on hardware lead time and security signoff.

Open items we promised to follow up on:
1) Hardware checklist (power/cooling, NICs, NVMe sizing) — Marcus will share suggested baseline.
2) Upgrade MOP (how to apply patches in an air-gapped environment) — I attached a short draft.
3) Acceptance tests and dry-run plan for on-site cutover.
4) Evidence for SOC2/access controls we discussed — Monica will prepare a short package.

Next steps / asks for Orion:
- Please confirm the preferred pilot window (2-day maintenance window) and your primary infra contact for scheduling (we have Priya and Alex on the thread).
- Share any appliance/rack constraints (U count, remote hands SLA, airflow) so Marcus can finalize the spec.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood-private-requirements.pdf (pdf, 238KB)]

I suggest we lock in a 30-minute follow-up on 11/24 to review Marcus' hardware recommendations and the draft MOP. If that works, Monica will send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni

Vivek — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifying questions from our infra team after the call:

1) Offline upgrades: can you summarize the exact steps and what we need to download into the air-gapped environment? Is there a signed bundle we can verify?
2) Rollback: if a patch causes issues, what is the typical rollback path and expected RTO for critical services?
3) Remote diagnostics: we cannot allow outgoing telemetry. Can Redwood provide a strictly inbound-only diagnostic channel (we'd prefer an ssh jumpbox model over outbound calls)?
4) On hardware: do you have a minimum/ recommended GPU/CPU and a preferred NVMe layout for KV cache? Our rack has 2x 42U stacks available; we'd like to map exact U requirements.

Pilot window: we prefer week of Jan 10, 2027 for a 2-day pilot. Priya will own scheduling.

Thanks — appreciate the attachments. Could Marcus include an alternate spec for a smaller pilot node (single-socket) so we can budget for both pilot and prod?

Alex Reynolds
CTO, Orion Bioinformatics
alex.reynolds@orionbio.com | +1 (650) 555-3489

Alex — good questions. High-level answers here and I'll let Marcus expand on the hardware specifics in a follow-up:

1) Offline upgrades
- We deliver a signed artifact bundle (SHA256 + PGP signature) that contains the runtime, model artifacts (if pinned), and a checksum manifest.
- Customer imports the bundle via USB or local transfer; the appliance verifies signatures locally; no outbound traffic required.
- Attachments include a short MOP draft showing the commands and verification steps.

2) Rollback / RTO
- We maintain a snapshot/rollback capability at the service layer; typical rollback times in our internal tests are 15–45 minutes depending on model sizes and KV cache warming strategy. We include a verification checklist to confirm service health post-rollback.

3) Remote diagnostics
- We support inbound-only diagnostic sessions via customer-initiated VPN/SSH. No phone-home telemetry is required. We can provide a documented process for an SSH jumpbox that Orion controls.

4) Pilot hardware options
- Marcus will attach two options: pilot (single-socket, 1xA40 equivalent or 1xH100 L4 low-end) and prod (dual-socket, 2xA100/H100 class). NVMe layout recommendations will be in his note.

Next step: Marcus, can you attach the two hardware profiles and a quick rack U mapping? Monica, I suggest we create the SOC2 evidence bundle next week and upload to the shared drive link.

Vivek

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T13:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — offline/on-prem qualification

Alex, Vivek — attaching two suggested hardware profiles and a compact rack map. High level notes below:

- Pilot (compact): single-socket AMD/Intel server with 1x GPU (A40 or comparable), 512GB RAM, 2x 2TB NVMe in RAID1 for OS and 2x 4TB NVMe for KV/cache. U footprint: 2U.
- Prod (redundant): dual-socket, 2x GPU (H100 class or 2x A100), 1–2TB RAM (workload dependent), 4x 4TB NVMe for distributed KV cache, redundant power supplies. U footprint: 4U–6U depending on chassis.

Other notes:
- Power/cooling: plan for 3.5–4 kW per rack slot for prod nodes with H100-class GPUs.
- Offline patch process: we provide a signed bundle with an installer that writes to a staging partition, runs validation tests, and then performs an atomic swap of the service symlink. If validation fails, the staging partition is discarded and the prior partition is reactivated.
- Acceptance tests: smoke (API responds), perf (sample workload run times), integrity (signature + checksum validation).

Attachments: [Attachment: hw-specs-suggested.csv (csv, 12KB)]

Happy to walk through rack maps on the 24th. Marcus
Principal Systems Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
